name: Texas Instruments
description: Texas Instruments makes analog chips (power management and signal conversion) and embedded processors (microcontrollers, processors, wireless connectivity, radar) and sells more than 80,000 products to electronics designers and manufacturers. Analog is 79 percent of revenue. It makes most of its own chips in its own fabs, including new 300mm wafer fabs in Texas and Utah, and more than 80 percent of revenue is sold directly (including TI.com) rather than through distributors. By end market, industrial and automotive are each about a third of revenue, personal electronics 21 percent and data center 9 percent. Cash funds a large dividend and buybacks.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label as shown on Wikipedia's List of S&P 500 companies (columns GICS Sector and GICS Sub-Industry). That page does not show the industry group or industry, so those are null rather than filled from memory.

hq.note: 12500 TI Boulevard, Dallas (FY2025 10-K Item 2); incorporated in Delaware

employees.note: About 33,000 employees worldwide, about 90% in R&D, sales or manufacturing (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Analog
businessLines.how: Chips sold per unit to electronics makers, most under direct relationships and some through distributors. Long product lives and high-volume reuse in customer designs; revenue follows industrial, automotive and electronics demand. Power and Signal Chain revenue is not split in the filing.
businessLines.description: Power (battery management, DC/DC and AC/DC regulators, power switches, multiphase controllers) and Signal Chain (amplifiers, data converters, interface, motor drives, clocks, sensing).

businessLines.name: Embedded Processing
businessLines.how: Chips sold per unit; customers invest their own software development on the parts, which tends to lock in multi-generation relationships.
businessLines.description: Microcontrollers, processors, wireless connectivity and radar products.

businessLines.name: Other
businessLines.how: Mix of chip sales and calculator/DLP product sales; operating profit here also includes items not allocated to segments (acquisition, restructuring, litigation and similar), so it is not a clean business margin.
businessLines.description: DLP products (projection), calculators (about 1% of revenue) and certain custom ASICs; also carries restructuring and corporate items.

brands.name: DLP
brands.share: Not separately reported; inside Other ($979M FY2025 with calculators and custom ASICs)

whatsNext.text: Acquisition of Silicon Labs for $231.00 per share in cash, enterprise value about $7.5B; closing expected in the first half of 2027, subject to approvals. A 364-day $5B delayed-draw term loan was arranged in June 2026 to fund it.
